CHAPTER 11
Nightgown
we have lain thus in bed chat and nap at short interval and Queequeg now and then affectionately throw his brown tattooed leg over mine and then draw they back so entirely sociable and free and easy be we when at last by reason of our confabulation what little nappishness remain in we altogether depart and we feel like get up again though day break be yet some way down the future

the more so I say because truly to enjoy bodily warmth some small part of you must be cold for there be no quality in this world that be not what it be merely by contrast
nothing exist in itself
if you flatter yourself that you be all over comfortable and have be so a long time then you can not be say to be comfortable any more
but if like Queequeg and I in the bed the tip of your nose or the crown of your head be slightly chill why then indeed in the general consciousness you feel most delightfully and unmistakably warm
for this reason a sleep apartment should never be furnish with a fire which be one of the luxurious discomfort of the rich
for the height of this sort of deliciousness be to have nothing but the blanket between you and your snugness and the cold of the outer air
then there you lie like the one warm spark in the heart of an arctic crystal
we have be sit in this crouch manner for some time when all at once I think I would open my eye for when between sheet whether by day or by night and whether asleep or awake I have a way of always keep my eye shut in order the more to concentrate the snugness of be in bed
because no man can ever feel his own identity aright except his eye be close as if darkness be indeed the proper element of our essence though light be more congenial to our clayey part
upon open my eye then and come out of my own pleasant and self create darkness into the impose and coarse outer gloom of the unilluminated twelve o’clock at night I experience a disagreeable revulsion
nor do I at all object to the hint from Queequeg that perhaps it be good to strike a light see that we be so wide awake and besides he feel a strong desire to have a few quiet puff from his Tomahawk
be it say that though I have feel such a strong repugnance to his smoking in the bed the night before yet see how elastic our stiff prejudice grow when love once come to bend they
for now I like nothing well than to have Queequeg smoking by I even in bed because he seem to be full of such serene household joy then

he gladly comply
though at the time I but ill comprehend not a few of his word yet subsequent disclosure when I have become more familiar with his broken phraseology now enable I to present the whole story such as it may prove in the mere skeleton I give
CHAPTER 12
Biographical
Queequeg be a native of Rokovoko an island far away to the West and South

CHAPTER 14
Nantucket
nothing more happen on the passage worthy the mentioning so after a fine run we safely arrive in Nantucket
Nantucket
take out your map and look at it
see what a real corner of the world it occupy how it stand there away off shore more lonely than the Eddystone lighthouse
look at it a mere hillock and elbow of sand all beach without a background
there be more sand there than you would use in twenty year as a substitute for blot paper
some gamesome wight will tell you that they have to plant weed there they do not grow naturally that they import Canada thistle that they have to send beyond sea for a spile to stop a leak in an oil cask that piece of wood in Nantucket be carry about like bit of the true cross in Rome that people there plant toadstool before their house to get under the shade in summer time that one blade of grass make an oasis three blade in a day ’s walk a prairie that they wear quicksand shoe something like Laplander snow shoe that they be so shut up belt about every way inclose surround and make an utter island of by the ocean that to their very chair and table small clam will sometimes be find adhere as to the back of sea turtle
but these extravaganza only show that Nantucket be no Illinois
look now at the wondrous traditional story of how this island be settle by the red man
thus go the legend
in olden time an eagle swoop down upon the New England coast and carry off an infant indian in his talon
with loud lament the parent see their child bear out of sight over the wide water
they resolve to follow in the same direction
set out in their canoe after a perilous passage they discover the island and there they find an empty ivory casket,—the poor little Indian ’s skeleton
what wonder then that these Nantucketers bear on a beach should take to the sea for a livelihood
they first catch crab and quohog in the sand grow bolder they wad out with net for mackerel more experienced they push off in boat and capture cod and at last launch a navy of great ship on the sea explore this watery world put an incessant belt of circumnavigation round it peep in at Behring ’s strait and in all season and all ocean declare everlaste war with the mighty animate mass that have survive the flood most monstrous and most mountainous
that Himmalehan salt sea Mastodon clothe with such portentousness of unconscious power that his very panic be more to be dread than his most fearless and malicious assault
and thus have these naked Nantucketers these sea hermit issue from their ant hill in the sea overrun and conquer the watery world like so many alexander parcel out among they the Atlantic Pacific and indian ocean as the three pirate power do Poland
let America add Mexico to Texas and pile Cuba upon Canada let the English overswarm all India and hang out their blaze banner from the sun two third of this terraqueous globe be the Nantucketer ’s
for the sea be his he own it as emperor own empire other seaman have but a right of way through it
merchant ship be but extension bridge armed one but float fort even pirate and privateer though follow the sea as highwayman the road they but plunder other ship other fragment of the land like themselves without seek to draw their living from the bottomless deep itself
the Nantucketer he alone reside and riot on the sea he alone in Bible language go down to it in ship to and fro plough it as his own special plantation
there be his home there lie his business which a Noah ’s flood would not interrupt though it overwhelm all the million in China
he live on the sea as prairie cock in the prairie he hide among the wave he climb they as chamois hunter climb the Alps
for year he know not the land so that when he come to it at last it smell like another world more strangely than the moon would to an Earthsman
with the landless gull that at sunset fold her wing and be rock to sleep between billow so at nightfall the Nantucketer out of sight of land furl his sail and lay he to his rest while under his very pillow rush herd of walrus and whale

philologically consider it be absurd
some century ago when the Sperm whale be almost wholly unknown in his own proper individuality and when his oil be only accidentally obtain from the stranded fish in those day spermaceti it would seem be popularly suppose to be derive from a creature identical with the one then know in England as the Greenland or Right Whale

CHAPTER 33
the Specksnyder
concern the officer of the whale craft this seem as good a place as any to set down a little domestic peculiarity on ship board arise from the existence of the harpooneer class of officer a class unknown of course in any other marine than the whale fleet
the large importance attach to the harpooneer ’s vocation be evince by the fact that originally in the old Dutch Fishery two century and more ago the command of a whale ship be not wholly lodge in the person now call the captain but be divide between he and an officer call the Specksnyder
literally this word mean Fat Cutter usage however in time make it equivalent to Chief Harpooneer
in those day the captain ’s authority be restrict to the navigation and general management of the vessel while over the whale hunting department and all its concern the Specksnyder or Chief Harpooneer reign supreme
in the British Greenland Fishery under the corrupted title of Specksioneer this old dutch official be still retain but his former dignity be sadly abridge
at present he rank simply as senior Harpooneer and as such be but one of the captain ’s more inferior subaltern
nevertheless as upon the good conduct of the harpooneer the success of a whale voyage largely depend and since in the American Fishery he be not only an important officer in the boat but under certain circumstance night watch on a whaling ground
the command of the ship ’s deck be also his therefore the grand political maxim of the sea demand that he should nominally live apart from the man before the mast and be in some way distinguished as their professional superior though always by they familiarly regard as their social equal
now the grand distinction draw between officer and man at sea be this the first life aft the last forward
hence in whale ship and merchantman alike the mate have their quarter with the captain and so too in most of the american whaler the harpooneer be lodge in the after part of the ship
that be to say they take their meal in the captain ’s cabin and sleep in a place indirectly communicate with it
though the long period of a southern whaling voyage by far the long of all voyage now or ever make by man the peculiar peril of it and the community of interest prevail among a company all of whom high or low depend for their profit not upon fix wage but upon their common luck together with their common vigilance intrepidity and hard work though all these thing do in some case tend to beget a less rigorous discipline than in merchantman generally yet never mind how much like an old mesopotamian family these whaleman may in some primitive instance live together for all that the punctilious external at least of the quarter deck be seldom materially relaxed and in no instance do away
indeed many be the Nantucket ship in which you will see the skipper parade his quarter deck with an elated grandeur not surpass in any military navy nay extort almost as much outward homage as if he wear the imperial purple and not the shabbiest of pilot cloth
and though of all man the moody captain of the Pequod be the least give to that sort of shallow assumption and though the only homage he ever exact be implicit instantaneous obedience though he require no man to remove the shoe from his foot ere step upon the quarter deck and though there be time when owe to peculiar circumstance connect with event hereafter to be detail he address they in unusual term whether of condescension or in terrorem or otherwise yet even Captain Ahab be by no mean unobservant of the paramount form and usage of the sea
nor perhaps will it fail to be eventually perceive that behind those form and usage as it be he sometimes mask himself incidentally make use of they for other and more private end than they be legitimately intend to subserve
that certain sultanism of his brain which have otherwise in a good degree remain unmanifested through those form that same sultanism become incarnate in an irresistible dictatorship
for be a man ’s intellectual superiority what it will it can never assume the practical available supremacy over other man without the aid of some sort of external art and entrenchment always in themselves more or less paltry and base
this it be that for ever keep God ’s true prince of the Empire from the world ’s husting and leave the high honor that this air can give to those man who become famous more through their infinite inferiority to the choice hide handful of the Divine Inert than through their undoubted superiority over the dead level of the mass
such large virtue lurk in these small thing when extreme political superstition invest they that in some royal instance even to idiot imbecility they have impart potency
but when as in the case of Nicholas the Czar the ring crown of geographical empire encircle an imperial brain then the plebeian herds crouch abase before the tremendous centralization
nor will the tragic dramatist who would depict mortal indomitableness in its full sweep and direct swing ever forget a hint incidentally so important in his art as the one now allude to
but Ahab my Captain still move before I in all his Nantucket grimness and shagginess and in this episode touch emperor and king I must not conceal that I have only to do with a poor old whale hunter like he and therefore all outward majestical trapping and housing be deny I
oh Ahab
what shall be grand in thee it must need be pluck at from the sky and dive for in the deep and feature in the unbodied air

CHAPTER 35
the Mast Head
it be during the more pleasant weather that in due rotation with the other seaman my first mast head come round
in most american whaleman the mast head be man almost simultaneously with the vessel ’s leave her port even though she may have fifteen thousand mile and more to sail ere reach her proper cruising ground
and if after a three four or five year voyage she be draw nigh home with anything empty in she say an empty vial even then her mast head be keep man to the last and not till her skysail pole sail in among the spire of the port do she altogether relinquish the hope of capture one whale more
now as the business of stand mast head ashore or afloat be a very ancient and interesting one let we in some measure expatiate here
I take it that the early stander of mast head be the old Egyptians because in all my research I find none prior to they
for though their progenitor the builder of Babel must doubtless by their tower have intend to rear the lofty mast head in all Asia or Africa either yet ere the final truck be put to it as that great stone mast of theirs may be say to have go by the board in the dread gale of God ’s wrath therefore we can not give these Babel builder priority over the Egyptians
and that the Egyptians be a nation of mast head stander be an assertion base upon the general belief among archæologist that the first pyramid be found for astronomical purpose a theory singularly support by the peculiar stair like formation of all four side of those edifice whereby with prodigious long uplifting of their leg those old astronomer be will not to mount to the apex and sing out for new star even as the look out of a modern ship sing out for a sail or a whale just bear in sight
in Saint Stylites the famous christian hermit of old time who build he a lofty stone pillar in the desert and spend the whole latter portion of his life on its summit hoist his food from the ground with a tackle in he we have a remarkable instance of a dauntless stander of mast head who be not to be drive from his place by fog or frost rain hail or sleet but valiantly face everything out to the last literally die at his post
of modern stander of mast head we have but a lifeless set mere stone iron and bronze man who though well capable of face out a stiff gale be still entirely incompetent to the business of sing out upon discover any strange sight
there be Napoleon who upon the top of the column of Vendome stand with arm fold some one hundred and fifty foot in the air careless now who rule the deck below whether Louis Philippe Louis Blanc or Louis the Devil
great Washington too stand high aloft on his tower main mast in Baltimore and like one of Hercules pillar his column mark that point of human grandeur beyond which few mortal will go
admiral Nelson also on a capstan of gun metal stand his mast head in Trafalgar Square and ever when most obscure by that London smoke token be yet give that a hidden hero be there for where there be smoke must be fire
but neither great Washington nor Napoleon nor Nelson will answer a single hail from below however madly invoke to befriend by their counsel the distract deck upon which they gaze however it may be surmise that their spirit penetrate through the thick haze of the future and descry what shoal and what rock must be shun
it may seem unwarrantable to couple in any respect the mast head stander of the land with those of the sea but that in truth it be not so be plainly evince by an item for which Obed Macy the sole historian of Nantucket stand accountable
the worthy Obed tell we that in the early time of the whale fishery ere ship be regularly launch in pursuit of the game the people of that island erect lofty spar along the sea coast to which the look out ascend by mean of nailed cleat something as fowl go upstairs in a hen house
a few year ago this same plan be adopt by the Bay whaleman of New Zealand who upon descry the game give notice to the ready man boat nigh the beach
but this custom have now become obsolete turn we then to the one proper mast head that of a whale ship at sea
the three mast head be keep man from sun rise to sun set the seaman take their regular turn as at the helm and relieve each other every two hour
in the serene weather of the tropic it be exceedingly pleasant the mast head nay to a dreamy meditative man it be delightful
there you stand a hundred foot above the silent deck stride along the deep as if the mast be gigantic stilt while beneath you and between your leg as it be swim the huge monster of the sea even as ship once sail between the boot of the famous Colossus at old Rhodes
there you stand lose in the infinite series of the sea with nothing ruffle but the wave
the trance ship indolently roll the drowsy trade wind blow everything resolve you into languor
for the most part in this tropic whale life a sublime uneventfulness invest you you hear no news read no gazette extras with startling account of commonplace never delude you into unnecessary excitement you hear of no domestic affliction bankrupt security fall of stock be never trouble with the thought of what you shall have for dinner for all your meal for three year and more be snugly stow in cask and your bill of fare be immutable
in one of those southern whalesman on a long three or four year voyage as often happen the sum of the various hour you spend at the mast head would amount to several entire month
and it be much to be deplore that the place to which you devote so considerable a portion of the whole term of your natural life should be so sadly destitute of anything approach to a cosy inhabitiveness or adapt to breed a comfortable localness of feeling such as pertain to a bed a hammock a hearse a sentry box a pulpit a coach or any other of those small and snug contrivance in which man temporarily isolate themselves
your most usual point of perch be the head of the t gallant mast where you stand upon two thin parallel stick almost peculiar to whaleman call the t gallant cross tree
here toss about by the sea the beginner feel about as cosy as he would stand on a bull ’s horn
to be sure in cold weather you may carry your house aloft with you in the shape of a watch coat but properly speak the thick watch coat be no more of a house than the unclad body for as the soul be glue inside of its fleshy tabernacle and can not freely move about in it nor even move out of it without run great risk of perish like an ignorant pilgrim cross the snowy Alps in winter so a watch coat be not so much of a house as it be a mere envelope or additional skin encase you
you can not put a shelf or chest of drawer in your body and no more can you make a convenient closet of your watch coat
concern all this it be much to be deplore that the mast head of a southern whale ship be unprovide with those enviable little tent or pulpit call crow’s nest in which the look out of a Greenland whaler be protect from the inclement weather of the frozen sea
in the fireside narrative of Captain Sleet entitle a Voyage among the Icebergs in quest of the Greenland Whale and incidentally for the re discovery of the Lost icelandic Colonies of Old Greenland in this admirable volume all stander of mast head be furnish with a charmingly circumstantial account of the then recently invent crow’s nest of the Glacier which be the name of Captain Sleet ’s good craft
he call it the Sleet ’s crow’s nest in honor of himself he be the original inventor and patentee and free from all ridiculous false delicacy and hold that if we call our own child after our own name we father be the original inventor and patentee so likewise should we denominate after ourselves any other apparatus we may beget
in shape the Sleet ’s crow’s nest be something like a large tierce or pipe it be open above however where it be furnish with a movable side screen to keep to windward of your head in a hard gale
be fix on the summit of the mast you ascend into it through a little trap hatch in the bottom
on the after side or side next the stern of the ship be a comfortable seat with a locker underneath for umbrella comforter and coat
in front be a leather rack in which to keep your speaking trumpet pipe telescope and other nautical convenience
when Captain Sleet in person stand his mast head in this crow’s nest of his he tell we that he always have a rifle with he also fix in the rack together with a powder flask and shoot for the purpose of pop off the stray narwhale or vagrant sea unicorn infest those water for you can not successfully shoot at they from the deck owe to the resistance of the water but to shoot down upon they be a very different thing
now it be plainly a labor of love for Captain Sleet to describe as he do all the little detailed convenience of his crow’s nest but though he so enlarge upon many of these and though he treat we to a very scientific account of his experiment in this crow’s nest with a small compass he keep there for the purpose of counteract the error result from what be call the local attraction of all binnacle magnet an error ascribable to the horizontal vicinity of the iron in the ship ’s plank and in the Glacier ’s case perhaps to there having be so many break down blacksmith among her crew I say that though the Captain be very discreet and scientific here yet for all his learn binnacle deviation azimuth compass observation and approximate error he know very well Captain Sleet that he be not so much immerse in those profound magnetic meditation as to fail be attract occasionally towards that well replenish little case bottle so nicely tuck in on one side of his crow ’s nest within easy reach of his hand
though upon the whole I greatly admire and even love the brave the honest and learn Captain yet I take it very ill of he that he should so utterly ignore that case bottle see what a faithful friend and comforter it must have be while with mittened finger and hooded head he be study the mathematic aloft there in that bird ’s nest within three or four perch of the pole
but if we southern whale fisher be not so snugly house aloft as Captain Sleet and his Greenlandmen be yet that disadvantage be greatly counter balanced by the widely contrast serenity of those seductive sea in which we south fisher mostly float
for one I use to lounge up the rigging very leisurely rest in the top to have a chat with Queequeg or any one else off duty whom I might find there then ascend a little way far and throw a lazy leg over the top sail yard take a preliminary view of the watery pasture and so at last mount to my ultimate destination
let I make a clean breast of it here and frankly admit that I keep but sorry guard
with the problem of the universe revolve in I how could I be leave completely to myself at such a thought engendering altitude how could I but lightly hold my obligation to observe all whale ship standing order keep your weather eye open and sing out every time
and let I in this place movingly admonish you ye ship owner of Nantucket
beware of enlist in your vigilant fishery any lad with lean brow and hollow eye give to unseasonable meditativeness and who offer to ship with the Phædon instead of Bowditch in his head
beware of such an one I say your whale must be see before they can be kill and this sunken eyed young Platonist will tow you ten wake round the world and never make you one pint of sperm the rich
nor be these monition at all unneeded
for nowadays the whale fishery furnish an asylum for many romantic melancholy and absent minded young man disgust with the carking care of earth and seek sentiment in tar and blubber
Childe Harold not unfrequently perch himself upon the mast head of some luckless disappointed whale ship and in moody phrase ejaculate
roll on thou deep and dark blue ocean roll
ten thousand blubber hunter sweep over thee in vain
very often do the captain of such ship take those absent minded young philosopher to task upbraid they with not feel sufficient interest in the voyage half hint that they be so hopelessly lose to all honorable ambition as that in their secret soul they would rather not see whale than otherwise
but all in vain those young platonist have a notion that their vision be imperfect they be short sighted what use then to strain the visual nerve
they have leave their opera glass at home
why thou monkey say a harpooneer to one of these lad we ’ve be cruise now hard upon three year and thou hast not raise a whale yet
whale be scarce as hen ’s tooth whenever thou art up here
perhaps they be or perhaps there might have be shoal of they in the far horizon but lull into such an opium like listlessness of vacant unconscious reverie be this absent minded youth by the blending cadence of wave with thought that at last he lose his identity take the mystic ocean at his foot for the visible image of that deep blue bottomless soul pervade mankind and nature and every strange half see gliding beautiful thing that elude he every dimly discover uprise fin of some undiscernible form seem to he the embodiment of those elusive thought that only people the soul by continually flit through it
in this enchant mood thy spirit ebb away to whence it come become diffused through time and space like Cranmer ’s sprinkle pantheistic ash form at last a part of every shore the round globe over
there be no life in thee now except that rock life impart by a gently rolling ship by she borrow from the sea by the sea from the inscrutable tide of God
but while this sleep this dream be on ye move your foot or hand an inch slip your hold at all and your identity come back in horror
over descartian vortex you hover
and perhaps at mid day in the fair weather with one half throttle shriek you drop through that transparent air into the summer sea no more to rise for ever
heed it well ye Pantheists

CHAPTER 60
the line
with reference to the whale scene shortly to be describe as well as for the well understanding of all similar scene elsewhere present I have here to speak of the magical sometimes horrible whale line
the line originally use in the fishery be of the good hemp slightly vapore with tar not impregnate with it as in the case of ordinary rope for while tar as ordinarily use make the hemp more pliable to the rope maker and also render the rope itself more convenient to the sailor for common ship use yet not only would the ordinary quantity too much stiffen the whale line for the close coiling to which it must be subject but as most seaman be begin to learn tar in general by no means add to the rope ’s durability or strength however much it may give it compactness and gloss
of late year the Manilla rope have in the american fishery almost entirely supersede hemp as a material for whale line for though not so durable as hemp it be strong and far more soft and elastic and I will add since there be an æsthetic in all thing be much more handsome and become to the boat than hemp
Hemp be a dusky dark fellow a sort of Indian but Manilla be as a golden haired Circassian to behold
the whale line be only two third of an inch in thickness
at first sight you would not think it so strong as it really be
by experiment its one and fifty yarn will each suspend a weight of one hundred and twenty pound so that the whole rope will bear a strain nearly equal to three ton
in length the common sperm whale line measure something over two hundred fathom
towards the stern of the boat it be spirally coil away in the tub not like the worm pipe of a still though but so as to form one round cheese shape mass of densely bedded sheaf or layer of concentric spiralization without any hollow but the heart or minute vertical tube form at the axis of the cheese
as the least tangle or kink in the coiling would in run out infallibly take somebody ’s arm leg or entire body off the utmost precaution be use in stow the line in its tub
some harpooneer will consume almost an entire morning in this business carry the line high aloft and then reeve it downwards through a block towards the tub so as in the act of coil to free it from all possible wrinkle and twist
in the english boat two tub be use instead of one the same line be continuously coil in both tub
there be some advantage in this because these twin tub be so small they fit more readily into the boat and do not strain it so much whereas the american tub nearly three foot in diameter and of proportionate depth make a rather bulky freight for a craft whose plank be but one half inch in thickness for the bottom of the whale boat be like critical ice which will bear up a considerable distribute weight but not very much of a concentrated one
when the paint canvas cover be clap on the american line tub the boat look as if it be pull off with a prodigious great wedding cake to present to the whale
both end of the line be expose the low end terminate in an eye splice or loop come up from the bottom against the side of the tub and hang over its edge completely disengage from everything
this arrangement of the low end be necessary on two account
first in order to facilitate the fastening to it of an additional line from a neighboring boat in case the stricken whale should sound so deep as to threaten to carry off the entire line originally attach to the harpoon
in these instance the whale of course be shift like a mug of ale as it be from the one boat to the other though the first boat always hover at hand to assist its consort
second this arrangement be indispensable for common safety ’s sake for be the low end of the line in any way attach to the boat and be the whale then to run the line out to the end almost in a single smoking minute as he sometimes do he would not stop there for the doom boat would infallibly be drag down after he into the profundity of the sea and in that case no town crier would ever find she again
before lower the boat for the chase the upper end of the line be take aft from the tub and pass round the loggerhead there be again carry forward the entire length of the boat rest crosswise upon the loom or handle of every man ’s oar so that it jog against his wrist in rowing and also pass between the man as they alternately sit at the opposite gunwale to the leaded chock or groove in the extreme pointed prow of the boat where a wooden pin or skewer the size of a common quill prevent it from slip out
from the chock it hang in a slight festoon over the bow and be then pass inside the boat again and some ten or twenty fathom call box line be coil upon the box in the bow it continue its way to the gunwale still a little further aft and be then attach to the short warp the rope which be immediately connect with the harpoon but previous to that connexion the short warp go through sundry mystification too tedious to detail
thus the whale line fold the whole boat in its complicated coil twisting and writhe around it in almost every direction
all the oarsman be involve in its perilous contortion so that to the timid eye of the landsman they seem as indian juggler with the deadly snake sportively festoon their limb
nor can any son of mortal woman for the first time seat himself amid those hempen intricacy and while strain his utmost at the oar bethink he that at any unknown instant the harpoon may be dart and all these horrible contortion be put in play like ring lightning he can not be thus circumstance without a shudder that make the very marrow in his bone to quiver in he like a shake jelly
yet habit strange thing
what can not habit accomplish?—gayer sally more merry mirth well joke and bright repartee you never hear over your mahogany than you will hear over the half inch white cedar of the whale boat when thus hang in hangman ’s noose and like the six burgher of Calais before King Edward the six man compose the crew pull into the jaw of death with a halter around every neck as you may say
perhaps a very little thought will now enable you to account for those repeat whaling disaster some few of which be casually chronicle of this man or that man be take out of the boat by the line and lose
for when the line be dart out to be seat then in the boat be like be seat in the midst of the manifold whizzing of a steam engine in full play when every fly beam and shaft and wheel be graze you
it be bad for you can not sit motionless in the heart of these peril because the boat be rock like a cradle and you be pitch one way and the other without the slight warning and only by a certain self adjust buoyancy and simultaneousness of volition and action can you escape be make a Mazeppa of and run away with where the all see sun himself could never pierce you out
again as the profound calm which only apparently precede and prophesie of the storm be perhaps more awful than the storm itself for indeed the calm be but the wrapper and envelope of the storm and contain it in itself as the seemingly harmless rifle hold the fatal powder and the ball and the explosion so the graceful repose of the line as it silently serpentine about the oarsman before be bring into actual play this be a thing which carry more of true terror than any other aspect of this dangerous affair
but why say more
all man live envelop in whale line
all be bear with halter round their neck but it be only when catch in the swift sudden turn of death that mortal realize the silent subtle ever present peril of life
and if you be a philosopher though seat in the whale boat you would not at heart feel one whit more of terror than though seat before your evening fire with a poker and not a harpoon by your side

the Whale as a dish
that mortal man should feed upon the creature that feed his lamp and like Stubb eat he by his own light as you may say this seem so outlandish a thing that one must need go a little into the history and philosophy of it
it be upon record that three century ago the tongue of the Right Whale be esteem a great delicacy in France and command large price there
also that in Henry VIIIth ’s time a certain cook of the court obtain a handsome reward for invent an admirable sauce to be eat with barbacued porpoise which you remember be a species of whale

the old monk of Dunfermline be very fond of they
they have a great porpoise grant from the crown

CHAPTER 66
the Shark Massacre
when in the Southern Fishery a capture Sperm Whale after long and weary toil be bring alongside late at night it be not as a general thing at least customary to proceed at once to the business of cut he in

and thus the work proceed the two tackle hoist and lower simultaneously both whale and windlass heaving the heaver singing the blubber room gentleman coil the mate scarfing the ship strain and all hand swear occasionally by way of assuage the general friction
CHAPTER 68
the Blanket
I have give no small attention to that not unvexed subject the skin of the whale
I have have controversy about it with experienced whaleman afloat and learn naturalist ashore
my original opinion remain unchanged but it be only an opinion
the question be what and where be the skin of the whale
already you know what his blubber be
that blubber be something of the consistence of firm close grain beef but tough more elastic and compact and range from eight or ten to twelve and fifteen inch in thickness
now however preposterous it may at first seem to talk of any creature ’s skin as be of that sort of consistence and thickness yet in point of fact these be no argument against such a presumption because you can not raise any other dense enveloping layer from the whale ’s body but that same blubber and the outermost enveloping layer of any animal if reasonably dense what can that be but the skin
true from the unmarred dead body of the whale you may scrape off with your hand an infinitely thin transparent substance somewhat resemble the thin shred of isinglass only it be almost as flexible and soft as satin that be previous to be dry when it not only contract and thicken but become rather hard and brittle
I have several such dried bit which I use for mark in my whale book
it be transparent as I say before and be lay upon the print page I have sometimes please myself with fancy it exert a magnifying influence
at any rate it be pleasant to read about whale through their own spectacle as you may say
but what I be drive at here be this
that same infinitely thin isinglass substance which I admit invest the entire body of the whale be not so much to be regard as the skin of the creature as the skin of the skin so to speak for it be simply ridiculous to say that the proper skin of the tremendous whale be thin and more tender than the skin of a new bear child
but no more of this
assume the blubber to be the skin of the whale then when this skin as in the case of a very large Sperm Whale will yield the bulk of one hundred barrel of oil and when it be consider that in quantity or rather weight that oil in its express state be only three fourth and not the entire substance of the coat some idea may hence be have of the enormousness of that animate mass a mere part of whose mere integument yield such a lake of liquid as that
reckon ten barrel to the ton you have ten ton for the net weight of only three quarter of the stuff of the whale ’s skin
in life the visible surface of the Sperm Whale be not the least among the many marvel he present
almost invariably it be all over obliquely cross and re crossed with numberless straight mark in thick array something like those in the fine italian line engraving
but these mark do not seem to be impress upon the isinglass substance above mention but seem to be see through it as if they be engrave upon the body itself
nor be this all
in some instance to the quick observant eye those linear mark as in a veritable engraving but afford the ground for far other delineation
these be hieroglyphical that be if you call those mysterious cypher on the wall of pyramid hieroglyphic then that be the proper word to use in the present connexion
by my retentive memory of the hieroglyphic upon one Sperm Whale in particular I be much strike with a plate represent the old indian character chisel on the famous hieroglyphic palisade on the bank of the Upper Mississippi
like those mystic rock too the mystic mark whale remain undecipherable
this allusion to the indian rock remind I of another thing
besides all the other phenomenon which the exterior of the Sperm Whale present he not seldom display the back and more especially his flank efface in great part of the regular linear appearance by reason of numerous rude scratch altogether of an irregular random aspect
I should say that those New England rock on the sea coast which Agassiz imagine to bear the mark of violent scrap contact with vast float iceberg I should say that those rock must not a little resemble the Sperm Whale in this particular
it also seem to I that such scratch in the whale be probably make by hostile contact with other whale for I have most remark they in the large full grow bull of the specie
a word or two more concern this matter of the skin or blubber of the whale
it have already be say that it be stript from he in long piece call blanket piece
like most sea term this one be very happy and significant
for the whale be indeed wrapt up in his blubber as in a real blanket or counterpane or still well an indian poncho slipt over his head and skirt his extremity
it be by reason of this cosy blanketing of his body that the whale be enable to keep himself comfortable in all weather in all sea time and tide
what would become of a Greenland whale say in those shudder icy sea of the North if unsupplie with his cosy surtout
true other fish be find exceedingly brisk in those hyperborean water but these be it observe be your cold blooded lungless fish whose very belly be refrigerator creature that warm themselves under the lee of an iceberg as a traveller in winter would bask before an inn fire whereas like man the whale have lung and warm blood
freeze his blood and he die
how wonderful be it then except after explanation that this great monster to whom corporeal warmth be as indispensable as it be to man how wonderful that he should be find at home immerse to his lip for life in those Arctic water
where when seaman fall overboard they be sometimes find month afterwards perpendicularly frozen into the heart of field of ice as a fly be find glue in amber
but more surprising be it to know as have be prove by experiment that the blood of a polar whale be warm than that of a Borneo negro in summer
it do seem to I that herein we see the rare virtue of a strong individual vitality and the rare virtue of thick wall and the rare virtue of interior spaciousness
oh man admire and model thyself after the whale
do thou too remain warm among ice
do thou too live in this world without be of it
be cool at the equator keep thy blood fluid at the Pole
like the great dome of St. Peter ’s and like the great whale retain o man
in all season a temperature of thine own
but how easy and how hopeless to teach these fine thing
of erection how few be dome like St. Peter ’s
of creature how few vast as the whale

CHAPTER 74
the Sperm Whale ’s Head contrast view
here now be two great whale lay their head together let we join they and lie together our own
of the grand order of folio leviathan the Sperm Whale and the Right Whale be by far the most noteworthy
they be the only whale regularly hunt by man
to the Nantucketer they present the two extreme of all the known variety of the whale
as the external difference between they be mainly observable in their head and as a head of each be this moment hang from the Pequod ’s side and as we may freely go from one to the other by merely step across the deck:—where I should like to know will you obtain a well chance to study practical cetology than here
in the first place you be strike by the general contrast between these head
both be massive enough in all conscience but there be a certain mathematical symmetry in the Sperm Whale ’s which the Right Whale ’s sadly lack
there be more character in the Sperm Whale ’s head
as you behold it you involuntarily yield the immense superiority to he in point of pervade dignity
in the present instance too this dignity be heighten by the pepper and salt colour of his head at the summit give token of advanced age and large experience
in short he be what the fisherman technically call a grey head whale
let we now note what be least dissimilar in these head namely the two most important organ the eye and the ear
far back on the side of the head and low down near the angle of either whale ’s jaw if you narrowly search you will at last see a lashless eye which you would fancy to be a young colt ’s eye so out of all proportion be it to the magnitude of the head
now from this peculiar sideway position of the whale ’s eye it be plain that he can never see an object which be exactly ahead no more than he can one exactly astern
in a word the position of the whale ’s eye correspond to that of a man ’s ear and you may fancy for yourself how it would fare with you do you sideways survey object through your ear
you would find that you could only command some thirty degree of vision in advance of the straight side line of sight and about thirty more behind it
if your bitter foe be walk straight towards you with dagger uplifted in broad day you would not be able to see he any more than if he be steal upon you from behind
in a word you would have two back so to speak but at the same time also two front side front for what be it that make the front of a man what indeed but his eye
moreover while in most other animal that I can now think of the eye be so plant as imperceptibly to blend their visual power so as to produce one picture and not two to the brain the peculiar position of the whale ’s eye effectually divide as they be by many cubic foot of solid head which tower between they like a great mountain separate two lake in valley this of course must wholly separate the impression which each independent organ impart
the whale therefore must see one distinct picture on this side and another distinct picture on that side while all between must be profound darkness and nothingness to he
Man may in effect be say to look out on the world from a sentry box with two joined sash for his window
but with the whale these two sash be separately insert make two distinct window but sadly impair the view

apply this spinal branch of phrenology to the Sperm Whale
his cranial cavity be continuous with the first neck vertebra and in that vertebra the bottom of the spinal canal will measure ten inch across be eight in height and of a triangular figure with the base downward
as it pass through the remain vertebræ the canal taper in size but for a considerable distance remain of large capacity
now of course this canal be fill with much the same strangely fibrous substance the spinal cord as the brain and directly communicate with the brain
and what be still more for many foot after emerge from the brain ’s cavity the spinal cord remain of an undecrease girth almost equal to that of the brain
under all these circumstance would it be unreasonable to survey and map out the whale ’s spine phrenologically
for view in this light the wonderful comparative smallness of his brain proper be more than compensate by the wonderful comparative magnitude of his spinal cord
but leave this hint to operate as it may with the phrenologist I would merely assume the spinal theory for a moment in reference to the Sperm Whale ’s hump
this august hump if I mistake not rise over one of the large vertebræ and be therefore in some sort the outer convex mould of it
from its relative situation then I should call this high hump the organ of firmness or indomitableness in the Sperm Whale

CHAPTER 89
fast fish and Loose Fish
the allusion to the waif and waif pole in the last chapter but one necessitate some account of the law and regulation of the whale fishery of which the waif may be deem the grand symbol and badge
it frequently happen that when several ship be cruise in company a whale may be strike by one vessel then escape and be finally kill and capture by another vessel and herein be indirectly comprise many minor contingency all partake of this one grand feature
for example,—after a weary and perilous chase and capture of a whale the body may get loose from the ship by reason of a violent storm and drift far away to leeward be retake by a second whaler who in a calm snugly tow it alongside without risk of life or line
thus the most vexatious and violent dispute would often arise between the fisherman be there not some write or unwritten universal undisputed law applicable to all case
perhaps the only formal whaling code authorize by legislative enactment be that of Holland
it be decree by the States General in A.D. 1695
but though no other nation have ever have any write whaling law yet the american fisherman have be their own legislator and lawyer in this matter
they have provide a system which for terse comprehensiveness surpass Justinian ’s Pandects and the by law of the Chinese Society for the Suppression of Meddling with other People ’s Business
yes these law might be engraven on a Queen Anne ’s farthing or the barb of a harpoon and wear round the neck so small be they
I. a fast fish belong to the party fast to it
II
a Loose fish be fair game for anybody who can soon catch it
but what play the mischief with this masterly code be the admirable brevity of it which necessitate a vast volume of commentary to expound it
first what be a fast fish
alive or dead a fish be technically fast when it be connect with an occupy ship or boat by any medium at all controllable by the occupant or occupants,—a mast an oar a nine inch cable a telegraph wire or a strand of cobweb it be all the same
likewise a fish be technically fast when it bear a waif or any other recognise symbol of possession so long as the party waife it plainly evince their ability at any time to take it alongside as well as their intention so to do
these be scientific commentary but the commentary of the whaleman themselves sometimes consist in hard word and hard knock the Coke upon Littleton of the fist
true among the more upright and honorable whaleman allowance be always make for peculiar case where it would be an outrageous moral injustice for one party to claim possession of a whale previously chase or kill by another party
but other be by no mean so scrupulous
some fifty year ago there be a curious case of whale trover litigate in England wherein the plaintiff set forth that after a hard chase of a whale in the northern sea and when indeed they the plaintiff have succeed in harpoon the fish they be at last through peril of their life oblige to forsake not only their line but their boat itself
ultimately the defendant the crew of another ship come up with the whale strike kill seize and finally appropriate it before the very eye of the plaintiff
and when those defendant be remonstrate with their captain snap his finger in the plaintiff tooth and assure they that by way of doxology to the deed he have do he would now retain their line harpoon and boat which have remain attach to the whale at the time of the seizure
wherefore the plaintiff now sue for the recovery of the value of their whale line harpoon and boat
Mr. Erskine be counsel for the defendant Lord Ellenborough be the judge
in the course of the defence the witty Erskine go on to illustrate his position by allude to a recent crim
con case wherein a gentleman after in vain try to bridle his wife ’s viciousness have at last abandon she upon the sea of life but in the course of year repent of that step he institute an action to recover possession of she
Erskine be on the other side and he then support it by say that though the gentleman have originally harpoon the lady and have once have she fast and only by reason of the great stress of she plunge viciousness have at last abandon she yet abandon she he do so that she become a loose fish and therefore when a subsequent gentleman re harpoon she the lady then become that subsequent gentleman ’s property along with whatever harpoon might have be find stick in she
now in the present case Erskine contend that the example of the whale and the lady be reciprocally illustrative of each other
these pleading and the counter pleading be duly hear the very learn judge in set term decide to wit,—That as for the boat he award it to the plaintiff because they have merely abandon it to save their life but that with regard to the controvert whale harpoon and line they belong to the defendant the whale because it be a loose fish at the time of the final capture and the harpoon and line because when the fish make off with they it the fish acquire a property in those article and hence anybody who afterwards take the fish have a right to they
now the defendant afterwards take the fish ergo the aforesaid article be theirs
a common man look at this decision of the very learn Judge might possibly object to it
but plough up to the primary rock of the matter the two great principle lay down in the twin whale law previously quote and apply and elucidate by Lord Ellenborough in the above cite case these two law touch fast fish and Loose Fish I say will on reflection be find the fundamental of all human jurisprudence for notwithstanding its complicated tracery of sculpture the Temple of the Law like the Temple of the Philistines have but two prop to stand on
be it not a saying in every one ’s mouth Possession be half of the law that be regardless of how the thing come into possession
but often possession be the whole of the law
what be the sinew and soul of russian serf and republican slave but fast fish whereof possession be the whole of the law
what to the rapacious landlord be the widow ’s last mite but a fast fish
what be yonder undetected villain ’s marble mansion with a door plate for a waif what be that but a fast Fish

what be the Archbishop of Savesoul ’s income of £ 100,000 seize from the scant bread and cheese of hundred of thousand of break back laborer all sure of heaven without any of Savesoul ’s help what be that globular £ 100,000 but a fast fish

what to that redoubte harpooneer John Bull be poor Ireland but a fast fish
what to that apostolic lancer Brother Jonathan be Texas but a fast fish
and concern all these be not Possession the whole of the law
but if the doctrine of fast fish be pretty generally applicable the kindre doctrine of Loose Fish be still more widely so
that be internationally and universally applicable
what be America in 1492 but a Loose Fish in which Columbus strike the spanish standard by way of waife it for his royal master and mistress
what be Poland to the Czar
what Greece to the Turk
what India to England
what at last will Mexico be to the United States
all Loose Fish

a reason for that ye lawyer

CHAPTER 92
Ambergris
now this ambergris be a very curious substance and so important as an article of commerce that in 1791 a certain Nantucket bear Captain Coffin be examine at the bar of the English House of Commons on that subject
for at that time and indeed until a comparatively late day the precise origin of ambergris remain like amber itself a problem to the learn
though the word ambergris be but the french compound for grey amber yet the two substance be quite distinct
for amber though at time find on the sea coast be also dig up in some far inland soil whereas ambergris be never find except upon the sea
besides amber be a hard transparent brittle odorless substance use for mouth piece to pipe for bead and ornament but ambergris be soft waxy and so highly fragrant and spicy that it be largely use in perfumery in pastile precious candle hair powder and pomatum
the Turks use it in cooking and also carry it to Mecca for the same purpose that frankincense be carry to St. Peter ’s in Rome
some wine merchant drop a few grain into claret to flavor it
who would think then that such fine lady and gentleman should regale themselves with an essence find in the inglorious bowel of a sick whale
yet so it be
by some ambergris be suppose to be the cause and by other the effect of the dyspepsia in the whale
how to cure such a dyspepsia it be hard to say unless by administer three or four boat load of Brandreth ’s pill and then run out of harm ’s way as laborer do in blast rock
I have forget to say that there be find in this ambergris certain hard round bony plate which at first Stubb thought might be sailor trowser button but it afterwards turn out that they be nothing more than piece of small squid bone embalm in that manner
now that the incorruption of this most fragrant ambergris should be find in the heart of such decay be this nothing
bethink thee of that saying of St. Paul in Corinthians about corruption and incorruption how that we be sow in dishonor but raise in glory
and likewise call to mind that saying of Paracelsus about what it be that maketh the good musk
also forget not the strange fact that of all thing of ill savor Cologne water in its rudimental manufacturing stage be the bad
I should like to conclude the chapter with the above appeal but can not owe to my anxiety to repel a charge often make against whaleman and which in the estimation of some already bias mind might be consider as indirectly substantiate by what have be say of the Frenchman ’s two whale
elsewhere in this volume the slanderous aspersion have be disprove that the vocation of whale be throughout a slatternly untidy business
but there be another thing to rebut
they hint that all whale always smell bad
now how do this odious stigma originate
I opine that it be plainly traceable to the first arrival of the Greenland whale ship in London more than two century ago
because those whaleman do not then and do not now try out their oil at sea as the southern ship have always do but cut up the fresh blubber in small bit thrust it through the bung hole of large cask and carry it home in that manner the shortness of the season in those Icy Seas and the sudden and violent storm to which they be expose forbid any other course
the consequence be that upon break into the hold and unload one of these whale cemetery in the Greenland dock a savor be give forth somewhat similar to that arise from excavate an old city grave yard for the foundation of a lie in Hospital
I partly surmise also that this wicked charge against whaler may be likewise impute to the existence on the coast of Greenland in former time of a dutch village call Schmerenburgh or Smeerenberg which latter name be the one use by the learn Fogo Von Slack in his great work on Smells a text book on that subject
as its name import smeer fat berg to put up this village be found in order to afford a place for the blubber of the dutch whale fleet to be try out without be take home to Holland for that purpose
it be a collection of furnace fat kettle and oil shed and when the work be in full operation certainly give forth no very pleasant savor
but all this be quite different with a South Sea Sperm Whaler which in a voyage of four year perhaps after completely fill her hold with oil do not perhaps consume fifty day in the business of boil out and in the state that it be caske the oil be nearly scentless
the truth be that live or dead if but decently treat whale as a specie be by no means creature of ill odor nor can whaleman be recognise as the people of the middle age affect to detect a Jew in the company by the nose
nor indeed can the whale possibly be otherwise than fragrant when as a general thing he enjoy such high health take abundance of exercise always out of door though it be true seldom in the open air
I say that the motion of a Sperm Whale ’s fluke above water dispense a perfume as when a musk scented lady rustle her dress in a warm parlor
what then shall I liken the Sperm Whale to for fragrance consider his magnitude
must it not be to that famous elephant with jewelled tusk and redolent with myrrh which be lead out of an indian town to do honor to Alexander the Great

a squeeze of the Hand

squeeze

CHAPTER 96
the Try Works
besides her hoist boat an american whaler be outwardly distinguish by her try work
she present the curious anomaly of the most solid masonry join with oak and hemp in constitute the complete ship

the Decanter
Ere the english ship fade from sight be it set down here that she hail from London and be name after the late Samuel Enderby merchant of that city the original of the famous whaling house of Enderby Sons a house which in my poor whaleman ’s opinion come not far behind the united royal house of the Tudors and Bourbons in point of real historical interest

the voyage be a skilful and lucky one and return to her berth with her hold full of the precious sperm the Amelia ’s example be soon follow by other ship English and American and thus the vast Sperm Whale ground of the Pacific be throw open

CHAPTER 103
Measurement of the Whale ’s Skeleton
in the first place I wish to lay before you a particular plain statement touch the live bulk of this leviathan whose skeleton we be briefly to exhibit
such a statement may prove useful here
accord to a careful calculation I have make and which I partly base upon Captain Scoresby ’s estimate of seventy ton for the large sized Greenland whale of sixty foot in length accord to my careful calculation I say a Sperm Whale of the large magnitude between eighty five and ninety foot in length and something less than forty foot in its full circumference such a whale will weigh at least ninety ton so that reckon thirteen man to a ton he would considerably outweigh the combined population of a whole village of one thousand one hundred inhabitant
think you not then that brain like yoked cattle should be put to this leviathan to make he at all budge to any landsman ’s imagination
have already in various way put before you his skull spout hole jaw tooth tail forehead fin and diver other part I shall now simply point out what be most interesting in the general bulk of his unobstructed bone
but as the colossal skull embrace so very large a proportion of the entire extent of the skeleton as it be by far the most complicated part and as nothing be to be repeat concern it in this chapter you must not fail to carry it in your mind or under your arm as we proceed otherwise you will not gain a complete notion of the general structure we be about to view
in length the Sperm Whale ’s skeleton at Tranque measure seventy two foot so that when fully invest and extend in life he must have be ninety foot long for in the whale the skeleton lose about one fifth in length compare with the live body
of this seventy two foot his skull and jaw comprise some twenty foot leave some fifty foot of plain back bone
attach to this back bone for something less than a third of its length be the mighty circular basket of rib which once enclose his vital
to I this vast ivory rib chest with the long unrelieved spine extend far away from it in a straight line not a little resemble the hull of a great ship new lay upon the stock when only some twenty of her naked bow rib be insert and the keel be otherwise for the time but a long disconnected timber
the rib be ten on a side

here be it say that this pertinacious pursuit of one particular whale continue through day into night and through night into day be a thing by no mean unprecedented in the South sea fishery
for such be the wonderful skill prescience of experience and invincible confidence acquire by some great natural genius among the Nantucket commander that from the simple observation of a whale when last descry they will under certain give circumstance pretty accurately foretell both the direction in which he will continue to swim for a time while out of sight as well as his probable rate of progression during that period
and in these case somewhat as a pilot when about lose sight of a coast whose general trend he well know and which he desire shortly to return to again but at some further point like as this pilot stand by his compass and take the precise bearing of the cape at present visible in order the more certainly to hit aright the remote unseen headland eventually to be visit so do the fisherman at his compass with the whale for after be chase and diligently mark through several hour of daylight then when night obscure the fish the creature ’s future wake through the darkness be almost as establish to the sagacious mind of the hunter as the pilot ’s coast be to he
so that to this hunter ’s wondrous skill the proverbial evanescence of a thing writ in water a wake be to all desire purpose well nigh as reliable as the steadfast land
